fit: barley in the usual-care arm and planned GAD-7
assessment: The NutriAct protocol names barley and barley flakes as usual-care foods and plans GAD-7. Parkinson disease is an exclusion example. The trial does not allocate boiled barley separately and the protocol contains no outcome results.

fit: freeze-dried parsley in a combined rat diet and stool mass
assessment: Both soup mixtures contained 5 g parsley per 100 g. They differed from the control in many foods and diet components. Fecal mass was higher in both mixtures. Fresh parsley, Parkinson disease and clinical constipation severity were not isolated.

fit: ungraded olive oil in a combined rat diet and stool mass
assessment: Both powders contain 5 g olive oil per 100 g, with oil grade unspecified. Both mixtures had higher fecal mass than the control. The multi-ingredient rat comparison does not isolate extra-virgin olive oil.

fit: olive oil in a Mediterranean pattern and separate bowel nutrition context
assessment: The review identifies olive oil in the Mediterranean diet and discusses bowel effects in relation to plant foods, fiber and water. No extra-virgin olive-oil bowel contrast is isolated.

fit: black tea constituent and isolated caffeine in Parkinson disease
assessment: In the review, black-tea polyphenols are a mechanistic lead. The reviewed clinical studies test isolated caffeine and do not compare brewed black tea for bradykinesia.

fit: tea risk and constituent context in Parkinson disease

fit: coffee context with indirect caffeine and overlapping symptom measures
